chapters.text: 子曰：「學而時習之，不亦說乎？有朋自遠方來，不亦樂乎？人不知而不慍，不亦君子乎？」
chapters.literal: 子曰 the Master said · 學 learn · 而 and then · 時 at the right times · 習之 practise it · 不亦說乎 is it not a delight? 有朋 to have friends · 自遠方 from far away · 來 come · 不亦樂乎 is it not a joy? 人不知 others do not know you · 而 and yet · 不慍 you do not resent it · 不亦君子乎 is that not a gentleman?
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'To learn, and at the right times practise it: is that not a delight? To have friends come from far away: is that not a joy? When others do not know you and you do not resent it: is that not a gentleman?'
chapters.note: A session line. 說 is read yuè here, 'delight' (later written 悅).

chapters.text: 有子曰：「其為人也孝弟，而好犯上者，鮮矣；不好犯上，而好作亂者，未之有也。君子務本，本立而道生。孝弟也者，其為人之本與！」
chapters.literal: 有子曰 Master You said · 其為人也 as for his way of being a person · 孝 filial · 弟 respectful to elders · 而 and yet · 好 likes · 犯上 going against superiors · 者 those who · 鮮 are rare · 矣. 不好犯上 not liking to go against superiors · 而 and yet · 好 liking · 作亂 stirring up disorder · 者 those who · 未之有 there has never been one · 也. 君子 the gentleman · 務 works at · 本 the root · 本立 the root set up · 而 and then · 道生 the Way grows. 孝弟 filial piety and respect for elders · 也者 as for · 其 surely · 為人之本 the root of being a person · 與
chapters.translation: Master You said: 'Few who are filial and respectful to their elders like to go against their superiors. Of those who do not like to go against their superiors, there has never been one who liked to stir up disorder. The gentleman works at the root; once the root is set up, the Way grows. Filial piety and respect for elders: are they not the root of being a person?'
chapters.note: 弟 stands for 悌 'respect for elders' (tì). 與 at the end is read yú. Text check: most editions (and ctext) read 為仁之本, 'the root of humaneness'. This source reads 人.

chapters.literal: 巧言 clever words · 令色 a pleasing face · 鮮矣 rare indeed · 仁 humaneness
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Clever words and a pleasing face: rarely are they humane.'
chapters.note: A session line. 鮮矣仁 puts 'rare' first for weight; the plain order is 仁鮮矣.

chapters.text: 曾子曰：「吾日三省吾身：為人謀而不忠乎？與朋友交而不信乎？傳不習乎？」
chapters.literal: 曾子曰 Zengzi said · 吾 I · 日 every day · 三省 examine on three points · 吾身 my person. 為人謀 in planning for others · 而不忠乎 have I not done my utmost? 與朋友交 in dealing with friends · 而不信乎 have I not kept my word? 傳 what was passed on to me · 不習乎 have I not practised it?
chapters.translation: Zengzi said: 'Every day I examine myself on three counts. In planning for others, have I failed to do my utmost? In dealing with friends, have I failed to keep my word? What was passed on to me: have I failed to practise it?'
chapters.note: Only the first clause is a session line. 為 is read wèi, 'for'. 傳 can also be 'what I pass on' to others.

chapters.text: 子曰：「道千乘之國，敬事而信，節用而愛人，使民以時。」
chapters.literal: 道 lead · 千乘之國 a state of a thousand chariots · 敬事 be respectful in affairs · 而信 and keep your word · 節用 be sparing in spending · 而愛人 and love the people · 使民 employ the people · 以時 at the right seasons
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'To lead a state of a thousand chariots: be respectful in handling affairs and keep your word; be sparing in spending and love the people; employ the people at the proper seasons.'
chapters.note: 道 stands for 導 'lead' (dǎo), and 乘 is read shèng, 'chariot'. 以時: call on the people's labour outside the farming season.

chapters.text: 子曰：「弟子入則孝，出則悌，謹而信，汎愛眾，而親人。行有餘力，則以學文。」

gloss.g: respect for elder brothers (悌 appears only here; 1.2 writes it 弟)
widely, to all (汎 appears only here)

chapters.literal: 弟子 a young man · 入 at home · 則孝 then is filial · 出 going out · 則悌 then respectful to elders · 謹 careful · 而信 and keeping his word · 汎愛眾 loving all widely · 而親人 and close to people. 行 doing this · 有餘力 has strength to spare · 則 then · 以學文 uses it to study culture
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'A young man should be filial at home and respectful to his elders when out; careful and true to his word; loving to all, and close to people. If he has strength to spare after doing this, let him use it to study culture.'
chapters.note: 弟子 here is 'a young man', not 'disciple'. Text check: most editions (and ctext) read 而親仁, 'draws close to the humane'. This source reads 人.

chapters.text: 子夏曰：「賢賢易色；事父母，能竭其力；事君，能致其身；與朋友交，言而有信。雖曰未學，吾必謂之學矣。」
chapters.literal: 子夏曰 Zixia said · 賢賢 treating the worthy as worthy · 易色 in place of [loving] looks · 事父母 serving father and mother · 能竭其力 able to use up all his strength · 事君 serving a ruler · 能致其身 able to give his very self · 與朋友交 dealing with friends · 言而有信 his word is to be trusted. 雖曰 even if it is said · 未學 he has not studied · 吾 I · 必 surely · 謂之學 call it learning · 矣
chapters.translation: Zixia said: 'Someone who values worth in place of good looks; who in serving his father and mother can give all his strength; who in serving his ruler can give his very self; whose word, with friends, can be trusted: even if they say he has not studied, I would surely call that learning.'
chapters.note: 賢賢易色 is disputed. 易 may be 'in place of' or 'make light of'; some read it of a husband who values his wife's worth over her looks.

chapters.text: 子曰：「君子不重則不威；學則不固。主忠信。無友不如己者。過則勿憚改。」
chapters.literal: 君子 the gentleman · 不重 is not grave · 則 then · 不威 has no awe · 學 his learning · 則 then · 不固 is not solid. 主 hold as the main thing · 忠信 loyalty and trust. 無 do not · 友 befriend · 不如己者 those not equal to you. 過 when you go wrong · 則 then · 勿 do not · 憚 shrink from · 改 correcting
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'If the gentleman is not grave, he does not inspire awe, and his learning is not solid. Hold to doing your utmost and keeping your word. Do not befriend those who are not your equal. When you go wrong, do not be afraid to put it right.'
chapters.note: 學則不固 is read two ways: 'his learning will not be solid', or 'if he learns he will not be rigid'. 無 here is 'do not', like 毋.

chapters.text: 曾子曰：「慎終追遠，民德歸厚矣。」
chapters.literal: 曾子曰 Zengzi said · 慎終 take care over the end · 追遠 follow up the distant · 民德 the people's virtue · 歸 returns · 厚 to fullness · 矣
chapters.translation: Zengzi said: 'Take care over the funerals of parents and keep up the sacrifices to distant ancestors, and the people's virtue will return to its fullness.'
chapters.note: 終 'the end' is a parent's death; 遠 'the distant' are the ancestors long gone.

chapters.text: 子禽問於子貢曰：「夫子至於是邦也，必聞其政，求之與？抑與之與？」子貢曰：「夫子溫、良、恭、儉、讓以得之。夫子之求之也，其諸異乎人之求之與？」

gloss.g: Ziqin, who asks Zigong about the Master

chapters.literal: 子禽 Ziqin · 問於子貢曰 asked Zigong · 夫子 the Master · 至於是邦也 arriving in a state · 必 always · 聞其政 hears about its government. 求之與 does he seek it? 抑 or rather · 與之與 do they give it to him? 子貢曰 Zigong said · 夫子 the Master · 溫 warm · 良 good · 恭 courteous · 儉 frugal · 讓 deferential · 以得之 by these gets it. 夫子之求之也 the Master's seeking it · 其諸 perhaps · 異乎 differs from · 人之求之 others' seeking it · 與
chapters.translation: Ziqin asked Zigong: 'When the Master arrives in a state, he always hears about its government. Does he seek this out, or is it offered to him?' Zigong said: 'The Master gets it by being warm, good, courteous, frugal and deferential. The Master's way of seeking it is perhaps different from other people's!'
chapters.note: 是邦 'this state': whichever state he comes to. 與 at a line end is a question mark (yú); 與之 is 'give it' (yǔ).

chapters.text: 子曰：「父在，觀其志；父沒，觀其行；三年無改於父之道，可謂孝矣。」
chapters.literal: 父在 while the father is alive · 觀其志 look at his aims · 父沒 when the father is gone · 觀其行 look at his conduct. 三年 for three years · 無改 makes no change · 於父之道 in his father's way · 可謂 may be called · 孝 filial · 矣
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'While a man's father is alive, look at his aims; when his father is gone, look at his conduct. If for three years he makes no change in his father's way, he may be called filial.'
chapters.note: 沒 is read mò, 'die'. The last sentence is 4.20 word for word.

chapters.text: 有子曰：「禮之用，和為貴。先王之道，斯為美；小大由之。有所不行，知和而和，不以禮節之，亦不可行也。」
chapters.literal: 有子曰 Master You said · 禮之用 in the use of ritual · 和 harmony · 為貴 counts as precious. 先王之道 the way of the former kings · 斯 this · 為美 was what was fine · 小大 small and great · 由之 followed it. 有所不行 there is where it does not work · 知和而和 knowing harmony and harmonizing · 不以禮 not by ritual · 節之 regulating it · 亦 also · 不可行 cannot work · 也
chapters.translation: Master You said: 'In the use of ritual, harmony is what counts most. In the way of the former kings this was what was fine, and small and great matters alike followed it. But there is where it does not work: to know harmony and simply harmonize, without regulating it by ritual, will not work either.'
chapters.note: 斯 'this' points back to 和 'harmony'. The last sentence warns against harmony sought for its own sake.

chapters.text: 有子曰：「信近於義，言可復也。恭近於禮，遠恥辱也。因不失其親，亦可宗也。」
chapters.literal: 有子曰 Master You said · 信 trust · 近於義 close to what is right · 言 your word · 可復 can be made good · 也. 恭 courtesy · 近於禮 close to ritual · 遠 keeps far · 恥辱 shame and disgrace · 也. 因 relying on · 不失其親 not losing those one should be close to · 亦 also · 可宗 can be looked up to · 也
chapters.translation: Master You said: 'When trust is close to what is right, your word can be made good. When courtesy is close to ritual, it keeps shame and disgrace away. If you rely on people without losing those you should be close to, you too can be looked up to.'
chapters.note: 復 is 'carry out, make good on' one's word. The last sentence is disputed; 宗 may be 'honour as head of the clan'.

chapters.text: 子曰：「君子食無求飽，居無求安，敏於事而慎於言，就有道而正焉，可謂好學也已。」
chapters.literal: 君子 the gentleman · 食 in eating · 無求飽 seeks no fullness · 居 at home · 無求安 seeks no comfort · 敏於事 quick in action · 而慎於言 and careful in speech · 就有道 goes to those who have the Way · 而正焉 and sets himself right by them · 可謂 may be called · 好學 fond of learning · 也已
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'The gentleman does not seek to eat his fill or to live in comfort. He is quick in action and careful in speech; he goes to those who have the Way and sets himself right by them. Such a man may be called fond of learning.'
chapters.note: 焉 at the end stands for 於之: 'by them'. 好學 is hào xué, 'love learning'.

chapters.text: 子貢曰：「貧而無諂，富而無驕，何如？」子曰：「可也；未若貧而樂道，富而好禮者也。」子貢曰：「《詩》云：『如切如磋，如琢如磨。』其斯之謂與？」子曰：「賜也，始可與言《詩》已矣，告諸往而知來者。」

gloss.g: to file bone or ivory (磋 appears only here)
to carve jade (琢 appears only here)
Zigong's personal name, which the Master uses

chapters.literal: 子貢曰 Zigong said · 貧 poor · 而無諂 and yet not flattering · 富 rich · 而無驕 and yet not arrogant · 何如 how is that? 子曰 the Master said · 可也 that will do · 未若 not as good as · 貧而樂道 poor and delighting in the Way · 富而好禮 rich and loving ritual · 者也. 子貢曰 Zigong said · 詩云 the Odes say · 如切如磋 as if cut, as if filed · 如琢如磨 as if carved, as if polished · 其 surely · 斯之謂 this is what is meant · 與? 子曰 the Master said · 賜也 Ci · 始 at last · 可與言詩 I can talk about the Odes with you · 已矣. 告諸往 tell him about what has gone · 而知來者 and he knows what is to come
chapters.translation: Zigong said: 'Poor without flattering, rich without arrogance: what do you think of that?' The Master said: 'That will do. But it is not as good as poor and delighting in the Way, rich and loving ritual.' Zigong said: 'The Odes say: as if cut, as if filed; as if carved, as if polished. Is this what it means?' The Master said: 'Ci, now at last I can talk about the Odes with you. Tell him about what has gone, and he knows what is to come.'
chapters.note: Text check: most editions (and ctext) read 貧而樂, without 道. The lines are from the Odes ('Qi yu'): bone and jade worked again and again until fine.

chapters.text: 子曰：「不患人之不己知，患不知人也。」
chapters.literal: 不患 do not worry about · 人之不己知 others' not knowing you · 患 worry about · 不知人 not knowing others · 也
chapters.translation: The Master said: 'Do not worry that others do not know you; worry that you do not know others.'
chapters.note: 不己知 puts the object 己 before the verb after 不, as 莫己知 did in 4.14.
